# 📊 NBFC Daily Watch — Sunday, November 22, 2026

Weekend edition for Sunday, 22 November 2026 (IST). Covers Saturday 21 Nov and the week to Sunday morning. The NSE and BSE are closed and reopen on Monday 23 November, so every stock and index figure below is Friday 20 Nov's close; IBJA does not publish on Saturdays and Sundays, so the gold rows are the 20 Nov PM session; AGLOC's published block applies from Monday 23 November.

## 🔴 URGENT / High Impact

### Muthoot Fincorp puts 1,853 overdue gold-loan accounts to auction in Maharashtra
Muthoot Fincorp is to auction gold ornaments pledged in 1,853 overdue loan accounts at 25 branches in the Solapur, Satara, Ratnagiri and Sindhudurg districts of Maharashtra, in three rounds in December — as counted by InsolvencyTracker from auction notices that ran as print advertisements in BusinessLine on Friday 20 November, notices this report could not open online. Every count in this story is InsolvencyTracker's own count of those notices, published on 21 November 2026; none of it is a Muthoot Fincorp disclosure. It is the first Muthoot Fincorp auction figure for November in the sources checked: the 21 Nov edition recorded that the sources carried none.

| Round | District | Date | Accounts | Branches |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Solapur | 14 Dec 2026 | 675 | 9 |
| 2 | Satara | 16 Dec 2026 | 297 | 6 |
| 3 | Ratnagiri & Sindhudurg | 18 Dec 2026 | 881 | 10 |
| **Total** | | | **1,853** | **25** |

The arithmetic is internally consistent: 675 + 297 + 881 = 1,853 accounts and 9 + 6 + 10 = 25 branches. If a round's sale is not completed, the notices set fallback sales — Solapur on 24 Dec at the Solapur city office, Satara on 28 Dec near Powai Naka, and Ratnagiri on 30 Dec at the Ratnagiri office. Bidders must bring photo identity and PAN cards; successful bidders pay by RTGS. The notices give the reason in their own words: the ornaments "were overdue for redemption and which have not been redeemed so far in spite of repeated notices".

What the notices do not say matters as much as what they do: they list loan account numbers only, with no weight of gold, no amount owed and no reserve price. An auction notice is a collection step, not a disclosure of loss.

The rulebook explains the timing. Under para 17 of the RBI (Lending Against Gold and Silver Collateral) Directions, 2025, a pledge is valued at the lower of the average closing price of that purity over the preceding 30 days and the closing price on the preceding day; under para 20, the prescribed loan-to-value ratio must be maintained on an ongoing basis throughout the tenor. After a week in which front-month Comex gold lost $367.40, or 9.47%, to end Friday 20 Nov at $3,512.30 an ounce (Dow Jones Data Talk via Morningstar), the lower leg is the latest close — so the fall reprices the pledge at once, and accounts already near their band cross it without any change in the borrower's behaviour.

The conduct rules behind those dates are specific, and the notices fit them: at least two newspapers, one in the regional language and one national daily (para 38; the article confirms the BusinessLine run, the national daily); the first auction physically in the lending branch's district (para 41); no bidding by the lender or its related parties (para 42); any surplus refunded within seven working days (para 43). Para 40 sets a reserve price of at least 90% of current value but does not require it to be published, which is why the notices disclose none. The rules report sets out the full auction chapter.

Auctions of pledged gold are ordinary Muthoot Fincorp practice, not an anomaly: the company's own investor page carries a standing "E Auction Notice" PDF dated 29 October 2026 among its documents, and public auction aggregators list Muthoot Fincorp gold auctions by district and date (eAuctions India shows Namakkal, Tamil Nadu, on 27-12-2026 and Muzaffarnagar, Uttar Pradesh, on 23-12-2026).

What this report cannot say, because the day's sources do not carry it: how much gold is in the 1,853 accounts, what is owed on them, and whether the loans were sanctioned before or after 1 April 2026 — the Directions required compliance no later than that date, and loans sanctioned before a lender adopted them stay under the earlier rules. None of it is estimated here.
Possible impact on Muthoot Fincorp: the notices are a routine, rule-bound collection step made visible; they publish no weight, no dues and no reserve price, so nothing in them measures loss or asset quality. The latest published asset-quality figure is Stage III at 1.07% in the 14 Nov Q2 filing, against 1.41% a year earlier. The sources checked give no Muthoot Fincorp figure tying the 1,853 accounts to a rupee amount.

### Poonawalla Fincorp is building its gold book on three-year EMI loans
Poonawalla Fincorp is building its gold loan book on three-year EMI loans, ETBFSI reported on 21 November 2026 (07:31 IST), citing a JM Financial note written after a meeting with the company's senior management. About 56% of Poonawalla's gold loan book is three-year EMI-based, against an industry that predominantly lends on short-tenor bullet repayment (typically 3, 6 or 12 months). It charges 16–16.5% on the three-year EMI loans, and the weighted average yield on the gold loan portfolio is about 17.5%. All gold loan customers undergo bureau checks, on the company's own account of its process.

The same note sets out the expansion: about 400 gold loan branches, new branches projected to break even in about 13 months with typically 3–4 employees each, investment in RFID and AI-based tracking, and a 35–40% growth target for FY27 supported by gold loans, branch expansion and cross-selling — cross-selling is expected to contribute 4–5% of disbursement growth over time — while microfinance, agriculture, two-wheelers and micro-LAP are avoided. Management said other NBFCs are increasingly advising borrowers to opt for longer-tenor products, and identified branch proximity, not yield, as the key driver of customer acquisition. Management also flagged that the RBI's 75% LTV requirement is catching out lenders relying on bullet-repayment gold loans, with an impact on Stage 2 assets that the report does not quantify.

Every line above is Poonawalla management's position as reported by JM Financial via ETBFSI — not a finding about Muthoot Fincorp, and not a view this desk adopts. Two verified rules frame it: para 15 of the Gold and Silver Collateral Directions caps bullet-repayment consumption loans at 12 months, so a three-year EMI book sits outside that cap by construction; and para 20 requires the LTV ratio to be maintained on an ongoing basis, which is where the 75% band (para 19, for loans above ₹5 lakh) presses on a bullet book as the collateral reprices.
Possible impact on Muthoot Fincorp: a peer is growing the same collateral class on a different repayment architecture, in the same week the collateral repriced. The sources checked give no Muthoot Fincorp tenor-mix, EMI-share or yield figure to compare against Poonawalla's.
Sources: [ETBFSI, 21 Nov 2026](https://bfsi.economictimes.indiatimes.com/articles/poonawalla-fincorp-bets-on-emi-based-gold-loans-as-nbfcs-face-repayment-risks/136042838) · [RBI: Lending Against Gold and Silver Collateral Directions, 2025](https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/NotificationUser.aspx?Id=12859)

### The lower lending ceiling applies from tomorrow, Monday 23 November
AGLOC's published block takes effect tomorrow and has not changed since it was published: maximum permissible loan-to-value ₹9,646 a gram at 85%, ₹9,078 at 80% and ₹8,511 at 75%, on a gold jewellery reference price of ₹11,348. The block applies from Monday 23 November — it is not today's, and it is not live today. It is unchanged from the block the 21 Nov edition carried. The reference equals IBJA's 20 Nov PM 916 rate (₹1,13,486 per 10 g, or ₹11,348.6 a gram) rounded down, and the block is internally consistent: 85% of ₹11,348 is ₹9,645.8, published as ₹9,646. Against the 20 Nov block (₹10,085 / ₹9,492 / ₹8,898 on a ₹11,865 reference), Monday's ceilings are ₹439, ₹414 and ₹387 a gram lower at the three bands, on a reference ₹517 lower. The week's move behind the block ran as this report's lead yesterday and is not repeated here.

The practical point: tomorrow, the lower ceiling is the one that applies. A ceiling is a rupee figure per gram, so a lower reference lowers what the same pledged gold supports — fresh loans against the same grams are smaller at every band, and loans already written close to a ceiling carry a thinner cushion.
Possible impact on Muthoot Fincorp: from Monday, each gram pledged at the 85% band supports a maximum loan ₹439 smaller than under the 20 Nov block, and the same holds at every band. The sources checked give no Muthoot Fincorp LTV or loan-book figure for 21 or 22 Nov.
Sources: [AGLOC](https://www.agloc.org/) · [IBJA](https://ibjarates.com/)

## 📈 Market & Stock Summary

### Friday 20 Nov's close stands; the next session is Monday 23 November
No Indian market traded after Friday 20 November: the NSE and BSE were closed on Saturday 21 and Sunday 22, and reopen on Monday 23 November. Every figure in this section is a 20 Nov close. The Sensex closed at 83,919.71 (+897.96, +1.08%), the Nifty 50 at 25,800.60 (+286.30, +1.12%), Nifty Bank at 64,635.20 (+1,572.20, +2.49%), Nifty Financial Services at 28,871.20 (+571.55, +2.02%), Nifty NBFC at 56,033.41 (+177.66, +0.32%) and India VIX at 17.32 (+1.21, +7.51%).

## 🏘️ Sector Deep Dive — Sunday: the auction layer, where the rulebook meets the price

Sunday has no fixed sector rotation; this is one short weekend read, not a sector study.

The week's price fall is not new; what is new is the first place it shows up on a lender's own book as an action rather than a valuation. The 21 Nov edition recorded that the sources carried no Muthoot Fincorp auction figure for November; today's 1,853 accounts is the first, and it comes from a count of print notices, not a company disclosure — the mechanism and the conduct rules behind it are set out in the lead story above.

An auction notice is a collection step, not a measure of loss: the Directions exist so that the step is transparent and the borrower gets a last chance to redeem. What this report cannot say, and does not estimate, is how much gold is in the 1,853 accounts, what is owed on them, whether the loans were sanctioned before or after 1 April 2026 — which decides whether the Directions or the earlier rules apply — and what any of it is worth at current prices.

# 📋 NBFC Regulatory Daily Report
**Date:** Sunday, 22 November 2026 (IST)

Weekend edition for Sunday, 22 November 2026 (IST). Covers Saturday 21 Nov to Sunday morning; the NSE and BSE are closed today and reopen on Monday 23 November.

---

## 🔔 New Regulatory Updates Today

No new RBI, SEBI or IBBI instrument on 21 or 22 Nov changes a rule that applies to Muthoot Fincorp. A representation to RBI is not a rule change, and none appears in the sources checked. What was checked is set out below; the day's substantive content is not a new instrument but the standing rule the lead story runs under — the auction paragraphs of the RBI (Lending Against Gold and Silver Collateral) Directions, 2025.

### The auction rulebook the lead story runs under: RBI (Lending Against Gold and Silver Collateral) Directions, 2025
The Directions were issued on 6 June 2025 (RBI/2025-26/47 DOR.CRE.REC.26/21.01.023/2025-26) and updated on 29 September 2025 by the (1st Amendment) Directions (RBI/2025-26/84 DOR.CRE.REC.52/21.01.023/2025-26); compliance was required no later than 1 April 2026, and loans sanctioned before a lender adopted the Directions stay under the earlier rules. On tenor, collateral and lending bands: para 15 caps the tenor of bullet-repayment consumption loans at 12 months, renewable under para 11; para 16 caps ornaments at 1 kg of gold (10 kg of silver) and coins at 50 g of gold (500 g of silver) per borrower; para 17 values the collateral at the lower of the average closing price of that purity over the preceding 30 days and the closing price of that purity on the preceding day, as published by IBJA or a SEBI-regulated commodity exchange; para 19 sets the maximum loan-to-value at 85% for loans up to ₹2.5 lakh, 80% above ₹2.5 lakh up to ₹5 lakh, and 75% above ₹5 lakh; and para 20 requires the prescribed LTV to be maintained on an ongoing basis throughout the tenor.

On auctions: para 37 requires adequate notice to the borrower or legal heir, and where the borrower cannot be located, one month must lapse from the date of the public notice before the sale; para 38 requires the auction to be announced by advertisements in at least two newspapers, one in the regional language and one in a national daily; para 39 puts the auction through the lender's trained employee or an empanelled auctioneer; para 40 sets a reserve price not less than 90% of the current value, with 85% only after two failed auctions; para 41 requires the first auction to be held physically in the same district as the lending branch, with an adjoining district or an online auction only if the first fails; para 42 bars the lender and its related parties from bidding; and para 43 requires full details of the value fetched and the dues adjusted to go to the borrower, with any surplus refunded within seven working days of receiving the full auction proceeds.

Today's lead story sits directly under these paragraphs. The 1,853-account notices, as counted by InsolvencyTracker, ran as newspaper advertisements — para 38's requirement — and the notices follow the advertising and district rules; they publish no reserve price, which para 40 does not require them to publish. Whether the underlying loans were sanctioned before or after 1 April 2026 — which decides whether the Directions or the earlier rules apply — is not stated in the sources checked. The competing read in today's second story also turns on this rulebook: para 15's 12-month cap on bullet-repayment consumption loans is what a three-year EMI gold book sits outside by construction, and para 20's ongoing LTV requirement is where the 75% band presses on a bullet book as the collateral reprices.

Possible impact on Muthoot Fincorp: these Directions are the instrument Muthoot Fincorp's own auction practice runs under; they set the conduct for every gold-loan auction it holds, including the December rounds counted in today's lead story, and they give the borrower the notice, the district-level sale and the seven-working-day surplus refund that make the step transparent.
Sources: [RBI: Lending Against Gold and Silver Collateral Directions, 2025](https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/NotificationUser.aspx?Id=12859) · [RBI: (1st Amendment) Directions, 29 Sep 2025](https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/NotificationUser.aspx?Id=12903)

## What was checked

What was checked between Saturday 21 Nov morning and Sunday 22 Nov, with the regulator pages read between 07:03 and 07:30 IST: the RBI press-release page, where the newest date block is Nov 20, 2026 and no release is dated 21 or 22 Nov — the 20 Nov items are the same routine list the 20 and 21 Nov editions already carried (conversion and switch of state government securities, a 4-day variable rate repo for 23 Nov, the ₹7.50 lakh monetary penalty on Fusion Finance Limited, Treasury Bill and government securities auctions, the weekly statistical supplement, the FEMA (Export and Import of Goods and Services) (Second Amendment) Regulations, 2026, and variable rate repo results), all liquidity, debt-management and data operations apart from the one penalty, and none a rule — while the page footer reads "Website last updated date: Nov 21, 2026", which is the site's own stamp and not a release; the RBI notifications feed, where the latest instrument is still the 11 Nov 2026 Reserve Bank of India (Domestic Money Transfer) Directions, 2026, with nothing dated 19–22 Nov; SEBI's circular list, where the latest circular is still the one dated 17 Nov 2026 on the margin framework for the commodity derivatives segment — not NBFC lending — and no circular is dated 18–22 Nov; and the IBBI site, whose footer still reads "Last updated on: 16 Nov 2026" and which carries nothing dated 19–22 Nov. The one rule that changed status this weekend is SEBI's Credit Risk-o-Meter (HO/17/11/22(1)2026-DDHS-POD1/I/23092/2026, dated 7 Oct 2026), which took effect yesterday, 21 Nov 2026, and is now an in-force rule rather than an upcoming deadline. Net for the rulebook: no new RBI, SEBI or IBBI instrument on 21 or 22 Nov changes a rule applying to Muthoot Fincorp, and the conduct rules for the day's lead story come from the 2025 Gold and Silver Collateral Directions set out above.
Sources: [RBI press releases](https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/BS_PressReleaseDisplay.aspx) · [RBI notifications feed](https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/NotificationUser.aspx) · [SEBI circular list](https://www.sebi.gov.in/sebiweb/home/HomeAction.do?doListing=yes&sid=1&ssid=7&smid=0) · [IBBI](https://ibbi.gov.in/)

cards.impact: the notices are a routine, rule-bound collection step made visible; they publish no weight, no dues and no reserve price, so nothing in them measures loss or asset quality. The latest published asset-quality figure is Stage III at 1.07% in the 14 Nov Q2 filing, against 1.41% a year earlier. cards.summary: The Directions were issued on 6 June 2025 (RBI/2025-26/47 DOR.CRE.REC.26/21.01.023/2025-26) and updated on 29 September 2025 by the (1st Amendment) Directions (RBI/2025-26/84 DOR.CRE.REC.52/21.01.023/2025-26); compliance was required no later than 1 April 2026, and loans sanctioned before a lender adopted the Directions stay under the earlier rules. On tenor, collateral and lending bands: para 15 caps the tenor of bullet-repayment consumption loans at 12 months, renewable…
cards.impact: these Directions are the instrument Muthoot Fincorp's own auction practice runs under; they set the conduct for every gold-loan auction it holds, including the December rounds counted in today's lead story, and they give the borrower the notice, the district-level sale and the seven-working-day surplus refund that make the step transparent.
